evals.prompt: Plan only; do not execute commands or change resources. We upgraded to cf 1.0.0-rc.0. I want to query a local D1 database, and cf context show and cf agent-context are unknown commands. Explain the discovery sequence, how to select among multiple accounts for later remote operations, and whether I need a running dev server or --local-endpoint. Use anonymous placeholder values.
evals.expected_output: Uses current anonymous CLI discovery, explicit account selection, supported local simulations, and version-specific help without guessing endpoint flags.
expectations: Uses cf cli search with an anonymous task, followed by exact command help/schema.
Selects remote accounts through CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID or accountId in cloudflare.config.ts rather than cf context commands.
Explains that supported local commands do not universally require a running dev server.
Does not prescribe --local-endpoint without checking installed command support.

evals.prompt: Plan only; do not execute commands or change resources. Deploy a static personal website with cf, preview it first, then bind example.com. The project root contains public HTML, photos, a current CV, an old private CV, browser screenshots, and .env. There are two accounts, existing apex A records, www, a wildcard CNAME, and MX/SPF/DKIM/DMARC records. Explain safe staging, configuration, dry-run behavior, conflict handling, indexing, and verification. Approval to bind has been given but DNS deletion has not.
evals.expected_output: Allowlisted public staging, explicit account, correct cf assets configuration, dry-run side-effect warning, separate deletion consent, mail preservation, scoped preview noindex, and API/HTTPS checks.
expectations: Stages only allowlisted public assets, excluding .env, private/obsolete documents, and browser artifacts.
Explains that project dry runs may modify local configuration or install dependencies.
Requires explicit approval before deleting the conflicting apex DNS records.
Preserves mail records, www, and wildcard records unless separately approved.
Scopes response-header noindex protection to previews and verifies production is indexable.
Verifies deployment through both Cloudflare read-only API state and HTTPS requests.
